items.e: In the name of God who counted those numbered above and below;I begin to explain according to the plain meaningthe Torah portion which begins with va-yedabber . IN THE WILDERNESS. This verse informs us that Moses did not go up to Mount Sinai since God’s glory was now present in the tent of meeting.

ON THE FIRST DAY OF THE SECOND MONTH. To tell him to arrange the standards and to instruct him how the Israelites were to journey and how they were to camp with reference to the tabernacle, for they journeyed on the twentieth day of the second month.

TAKE YE THE SUM. Se’u et rosh bene yisra’el (take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel) is similar to ki tissa et rosh bene yisra’el (when thou takest the sum of the children of Israel) (Ex. 30:12). I have explained its meaning there.
BY THEIR FAMILIES BY THEIR FATHER’S HOUSES. For pedigree is not determined by the mother.
BY THEIR POLLS. I have already explained the meaning of gulgelotam (their polls).
IN ISRAEL. This excludes the mixed multitude.

EVERY ONE HEAD OF HIS FATHERS’ HOUSE. Ish rosh le-vet avotav (every one head of his fathers’ house) is an abridged phrase. The text should have read, ish ish rosh le-vet avotav (every one head of his fathers’ house).
OF REUBEN. Scripture begins with Jacob’s first-born, as it is stated, yet not so that he was to be reckoned in the genealogy as first-born (I Chron. 5:1).

OF THE CHILDREN OF JOSEPH. The children of Joseph are mentioned after the children of Leah because Rachel’s status was greater than that of the handmaids. Scripture begins with Ephraim, in keeping with the actions of our father Jacob. Scripture places Ephraim and Manasseh before Benjamin because they are in place of Joseph. Scripture then begins with Dan, who was the first-born of the handmaids. Asher follows Dan because God knew that Asher would be the head of those who camp under the standard of Dan. Scripture then mentions Gad because he was the first-born of Leah’s handmaid.
THESE WERE THE ELECT OF THE CONGREGATION. The meaning of keru’e ha-edah (the elect of the congregation) is that the congregation does nothing unless they are called.
THE TRIBES OF THEIR FATHERS. The meaning of mattot avotam is the tribes of their fathers. Thus each one was prince of a tribe.
THEY WERE THE HEADS OF THE THOUSANDS OF ISRAEL. Each one was a leader over all the thousands that comprised a tribe, for there was also a chief over one thousand.
AND MOSES AND AARON TOOK. With them.
THAT ARE POINTED OUT BY NAME. Nikkevu means that are pointed out. Compare, yikkvennu (mark out) in Which the mouth of the Lord shall mark out (Is. 62:2).
AND THEY DECLARED THEIR PEDIGREES. They were asked for their birth dates, for only those from twenty and above were to be counted. Their progeny were then recorded.

SO DID HE NUMBER THEM. The reference is to Moses, who was the most important. Scripture begins with Reuben, as he was the first-born. Simeon is next because he was born after Reuben. Gad the first-born of Leah’s handmaid, follows. We thus have Reuben’s standard. Next comes the standard of Judah, followed by the standard of Ephraim and the standard of Dan. Those who camped around each standard did so in the same manner in which they offered the sacrifices dedicating the altar. Note, there were twelve tribes, for Levi was not counted and Joseph’s two sons were. Now the world has four sides. Behold, three tribes camped on each one of the four sides. Now Leah had five sons, for one of her six sons was not counted. She had two standards. They [Moses and Aaron] completed one of her standards with [Gad] the first-born of her handmaid. They placed Gad with the standard of Reuben, who was also a first-born. Judah made up the second standard [of Leah]. His younger brothers camped with him. Rachel had a standard of her own. Ephraim was in place of Joseph. He preceded Manasseh, in keeping with the words of Jacob. The fourth standard was that of Rachel’s handmaid. It was led by [Dan] her first-born. Asher followed even though he was younger than Naphtali. The son of Leah’s handmaid was so honored because the standard belonged to Rachel’s handmaid. If you look carefully into things, you will know that the south is the head and the north the tail. I cannot explain the aforementioned. Reuben was therefore placed in the south because he was the head. Dan was placed in the north. Observe, there was no one among the tribes comparable in might to Judah, who was compared to a lion’s whelp (Gen. 49:9), and to the tribe of Dan, who is likewise compared to a lion by Moses. These tribes were thus first and last. Scripture mentions by their polls (le-gulgelotam) with regard to Reuben and also with regard to Simeon to show that it was the same case with the other tribes, for Scripture was being brief.

[AND ALL THOSE THAT WERE NUMBERED OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL BY THEIR FATHERS’ HOUSES, FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD AND UPWARD.] It means that only those who were aged twenty and above were counted. Scripture then goes on to say, even all those that were numbered . The latter refers to their total number.
WERE NOT NUMBERED AMONG THEM. The word hotpakdu (were not numbered) is of two forms. It is both a hitpa’el and a hofal .
HOWBEIT THE TRIBE OF LEVI THOU SHALT NOT NUMBER. This explains were not numbered (v. 47), that the Levites were not numbered because this is what God commanded.
NEITHER SHALT THOU TAKE THE SUM OF THEM. Their total number, as I have explained.

BUT APPOINT THOU THE LEVITES OVER THE TABERNACLE. Scripture explains here why the Levites were not counted. They were not counted because the charge of the tabernacle was upon them. Therefore they did not serve in the army.
THE TABERNACLE OF THE TESTIMONY. The reference is to the tent of meeting and the tabernacle of the ark, which contains the testimony.
AND OVER ALL THE FURNITURE THEREOF. Such as the menorah, the table, and the altars.
AND OVER ALL THAT BELONGETH TO IT. The reference is the utensils which serve the furniture.

AND THEY SHALL BEAR THE TABERNACLE. They are the very ones who carry the tabernacle when the camp journeys, and they are the ones who shall minister unto the tabernacle when they camp. They shall camp around the tabernacle.
AND WHEN THE TABERNACLE SETTETH FORWARD, THE LEVITES SHALL TAKE IT DOWN. They shall remove its bars and posts. When the tabernacle rests, they shall set it up.
AND THE COMMON MAN. A person who is not a Levite, even if he is an Israelite. SHALL BE PUT TO DEATH. A law court shall put him to death.
[AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SHALL PITCH.] Its meaning is, “when” the children of Israel shall pitch.
EVERY MAN WITH HIS OWN CAMP. The meaning of every man is each tribe.
[AND EVERY MAN WITH HIS OWN STANDARD.] Its meaning is that the tribe of one standard shall not be mixed with the tribe of another standard.

BUT THE LEVITES SHALL PITCH ROUND ABOUT THE TABERNACLE OF TESTIMONY. Our verse explains why the earlier verse stated that the Levites were to encamp round about the tabernacle: so that no one from the congregation of Israel should draw close to the tabernacle and die. This is the meaning of that there be no wrath upon…the children of Israel , as there was in the case of Uzzah, who touched the ark.

Scripture there states, And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah (II Sam. 6:7). The meaning of upon the congregation of the children of Israel is, upon anyone from the children of Israel. It is similar to and was buried in the cities of Gilead (Jud. 12:7) and Even upon a colt the foal of asses (Zech. 9:9). There are many such cases.
AND THE LEVITES SHALL KEEP THE CHARGE. The Levites are obligated to guard the tabernacle.
THUS DID THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. They never touched the tabernacle.

[AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES AND UNTO AARON.] Scripture reads, unto Moses and unto Aaron because Aaron and his sons were to command the Kohathites as to which burdens they were to carry upon their shoulders.

ACCORDING TO THE ENSIGNS. There were signs upon each and every standard. The ancients said that the banner of Reuben had the form of a person on it. Their statement is based on a midrashic interpretation concerning the mandrakes found by Reuben. The ancients also tell us that there was an image of a lion on the standard of Judah, for Jacob had compared Judah to a lion. They also tell us that the banner of Ephraim had the image of an ox upon it, in keeping with the verse, His firstling bullock (Deut. 33:17). The flag of Dan had the image of an eagle. Thus the banners were similar to the cherubim which the prophet Ezekiel saw.
A GOOD WAY OFF. The word mi-neged means a good way off.
ON THE EAST SIDE TOWARD THE SUNRISING. The beginning of the east.
AND HIS HOST ( U-FEKUDEHEM ). Scripture could have read u-fekudav (and his host). There is no difference between the two terms.
AND THOSE THAT PITCH NEXT UNTO HIM. Ve-hachonim alav means those that pitch with him. Issachar was behind Judah and in front of Zebulun who was third.
THEY SHALL SET FORTH FIRST. The meaning of rishonah yissa’u is, they shall set forth first.
ON THE SOUTH SIDE. The word temanah (on the south side) comes from the same root as the word yemin (right).
SECOND. Sheniyyim (second) is an adjective.

THEN THE TENT OF MEETING, WITH THE CAMP OF THE LEVITES, SHALL SET FORWARD IN THE MIDST OF THE CAMPS. In the midst of the above-mentioned camps, for the Gershonites and Merarites journeyed between the banner of Judah and the banner of Reuben. And the Kohathites, and with them Aaron and his sons, journeyed between the banner of Reuben and the banner of Ephraim.

AS THEY ENCAMP, SO SHALL THEY SET FORWARD. The reference is to the camps , which refers to the camp of the Israelites. It does not refer to the camp of the Levites. The Gershonites, who pitched on the west of the sanctuary, and the Merarites on the north journeyed together, after the camp of Judah who pitched on the east.

EVERY MAN IN HIS PLACE. The meaning of al yado (in his place) is, in his corner and place. The same applies to yad ha-yarden (by the side of the Jordan) (Num. 13:29) and ve-yad tiheyah lekha (and thou shalt have a paddle) (Deut. 23:13).

THESE ARE THEY THAT WERE NUMBERED OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. When they journeyed, they were the same number as on the day that they were counted. Thus not one of them died in twenty days. This is a great wonder.
BUT THE LEVITES WERE NOT NUMBERED AMONG THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. Scripture makes it clear that we should not count even one Levite among those who were counted when they journeyed.
THUS DID THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. All the days that they spent in the desert.

NOW THESE ARE THE GENERATIONS OF AARON AND MOSES. Scripture states this because it wants to inform us that their offspring did not beget children and did not increase in close to ten months. God chose the tribe of Levi at the time God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, when Moses ascended to atone for the making of the golden calf. God then said to Moses, Bring the tribe of Levi near (v. 6). The Lord then also related all that is contained in the section that opens with And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel (v. 12). When the tabernacle was erected, God told Moses, Number the children of Levi (v. 15). God’s presence was then manifest in the tabernacle. Scripture therefore reads, in the wilderness of Sinai (v. 14). Now the descendants of Aaron and Moses in the wilderness of Sinai numbered the same as they did at Mount Sinai. However, two sons of Aaron were missing.I therefore said that the Levites did not give a ransom for their souls, for Scripture clearly states, for every one that passed over to them that are numbered (Ex. 38:26). Some say that Moses did not count the Israelites before the tabernacle was constructed. He knew their number only by way of prophecy. However, Scripture contradicts them. It clearly states, When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel (Ex. 30:11).
THE PRIESTS THAT WERE ANOINTED. With the anointing oil, for they were high priests.
[AND THEY HAD NO CHILDREN.] They did not leave behind any grown or small children. Therefore the Levites were lacking in number, for it is possible for the grown children to beget children.
IN THE PRESENCE OF. I have previously explained the meaning of al pene (in the presence of).

BEFORE AARON THE PRIEST. Who was the prince of the tribe. The meaning of ve-ha’amadt (and set them) is, that they may minister. As the Lord liveth, before whom I stand (amadti) (II Kings 5:16) is similar.
AND THE CHARGE OF THE WHOLE CONGREGATION. In the offering of sacrifices.
AND THE CHARGE OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. They will make sure that an Israelite does not enter the tabernacle.
THEY ARE WHOLLY GIVEN UNTO HIM. Forever. Or to them and their descendants who take their place.
UNTO AARON AND TO HIS SONS. Both those who are presently alive and those who will arise after them.
FROM THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. To be separated from the children of Israel.

AND THOU SHALT APPOINT AARON AND HIS SONS. His sons includes the sons of his sons. The meaning of and thou shalt appoint (tifkod) is, you shall appoint each one of them. The meaning of that they may keep their priesthood is that they not do anything that will disqualify them from being priests.

AND THE COMMON MAN THAT DRAWETH NIGH. To the priest, to serve as a priest. [SHALL BE PUT TO DEATH.] An Israelite or a Levite who serves as a priest shall be put to death. The chapter that opens with the words And I, behold, I have taken the Levites is also connected to the chapter which preceded it, for the Torah contains chapters that are separated but are connected by content. Similarly, Moreover the hand of the Lord was against them, to discomfit them from the midst of the camp, until they were consumed (Deut. 2:15), and, And it came to pass on the day when the Lord spoke unto Moses in the land of Egypt (Ex. 6:28).
AND I, BEHOLD, I HAVE TAKEN THE LEVITES. The Levites have been greatly elevated.
FIRST-BORN. Bekhor (first-born) is connected to peter (openeth).
AND THE LEVITES SHALL BE MINE. They shall be holy unto Me.
FOR ALL THE FIRST-BORN ARE MINE. Its meaning is, for also the first-born are Mine.
ON THE DAY THAT I SMOTE. This means at the time that I smote. There are many such cases.
MINE THEY SHALL BE. This means they are Mine and they shall be Mine, for all human first-born and similarly the first-born of unclean cattle shall be redeemed.

FROM A MONTH OLD AND UPWARD. Until the sun and moon are once again in conjunction, or until the moon returns to its approximate place of departure and its original position and its present place are near each other. The intelligent person will understand this.
GERSHON. For he was the first-born. In Chronicles the name is spelled with a mem in place of a nun (I Chron. 6:1).
OF GERSHON WAS THE FAMILY OF THE LIBNITES, AND THE FAMILY OF THE SHIMEITES. Its meaning is, these two families numbered the following amount.
BEHIND THE TABERNACLE. Achare (behind) means the same as achore (behind). Compare, achor va-kedem (behind and before) (Ps. 139:5).
WESTWARD. The term employed for westward is yamah because the great Spanish sea lies west of the Land of Israel.
THE TABERNACLE. The reference is to the ten curtains.
THE TENT. The reference is to the eleven curtains.
THE COVERING THEREOF. The covering which covered the cover is included.
WHICH IS BY THE TABERNACLE. Which is inside the court.
AND BY THE ALTAR. Which is outside the tabernacle.
[ROUND ABOUT.] Its meaning is that there was no place that was not enclosed; there was no opening that was uncovered.
EVEN WHATSOEVER PERTAINETH TO THE SERVICE THEREOF. I will explain this later.
KEEPERS OF THE CHARGE OF THE HOLY. The reference is to the ark. The ark, as I have previously explained, is referred to as the holy, in contrast to the tabernacle.

SOUTHWARD. Kohath was placed at the right because he was the most important of all the sons of Levi, and the right is more important than the left or the back. There is no side, with the exception of the east, more important. Gershon had an advantage over Merari, for Gershon was the first-born of Levi. Hence he carried that which was holy, in contrast to what Merari carried. Gershon therefore camped on the west, like the standard of Ephraim. Merari camped on the north like Dan, who was the son of the handmaid. Now the Kohathites camped next to the banner of Reuben. Korah therefore joined with Dathan and Abiram. I will explain this later.
AND THE ALTARS. Both of them.

AND THE VESSELS OF THE SANCTUARY WHEREWITH THE PRIESTS MINISTER. The reference is to the vessels of the menorah, the table, and the altars. Many erred in explaining the meaning of and the screen , and all that pertaineth to the service thereof . It is clearly true that the reference is to the screen of the door of the tent of meeting.
AND ALL THAT PERTAINETH TO THE SERVICE THEREOF. Its cords.

PRINCE OF THE PRINCES OF THE LEVITES. There were three princes of Levi. The term nesi’e (princes) in the phrase nesi’e ha-levi (princes of Levi) applies to the word levi and also to another word. It is like the word lo (not) in It is not the great that are wise (Job 32:9). The second part of our verse is to be interpreted as if written the princes having the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary . Its meaning is that these three princes had oversight over the keepers of the charge of the sanctuary, who were Levites.

NORTHWARD. It is possible that the word tzafonah (northward) is derived from the word tzafanta (laid up) in Thou hast laid up for them that fear Thee (Ps. 31:20) and from the word tzafon (laid up) in laid up for the righteous (Prov. 13:22). The north is so called because there is nothing in the south.

EASTWARD…TOWARD THE SUNRISING. Mizrachah means toward the sunrising. It refers to the place where the circles come together. Observe, the tent of Moses, the tent of Aaron, and the tent of his children and his children’s children and all their entire households were in the east.
AND THE COMMON MAN THAT DREW NIGH. To the holy place. Note, all the Levites camped around the tabernacle in order to guard it.

WERE TWENTY AND TWO THOUSAND. In all. When you add up the figures you will find that they come to three hundred above the figure given in Scripture. Some say that Scripture is being brief and mentions only the thousands and neglects the hundreds. However, this cannot be the case. Scripture mentions less than three hundred over and above a round number. The truth is in accordance with tradition which states that a first-born does not free a first-born. The meaning of our verse thus is, all that were numbered of the Levites with the exception of the first-born [were twenty and two thousand]. Judah the Persian calculated to prove, from the number that the first-born of the Levites were one seventy-third of the Levites. He went on to say that if you divide the number of Israelites by seventy-three, and take the number of Levites who came to serve in the tabernacle rather than the number of Levites age one month and above, then the number will be close. However, all this is nothing. The Israelites were counted from twenty and above. No other fixed unit was used. However, the Levites were counted from twenty to fifty. There is a large difference between them. We will rely only on tradition.
NUMBER ALL THE FIRST-BORN MALES. Note that males is an adjective.
AND THE CATTLE OF THE LEVITES. So that the Levites do not lose. The firstlings among the cattle are also for the Lord.

TAKE THE LEVITES. A second time. It is as if it stated, when you take the Levites, then those who are over and above will be redeemed. The word peduye (redemption of) is connected to the number. There are many other such instances. The disputers say that here we learn that the redemption price of every first-born is five shekels. However, there is no proof here, for this commandment stands by itself. The truth is in keeping with tradition.
REDEMPTION. Pidyom (redemption) is spelled with a mem in place of a nun . Compare, Gershon.
TAKE THE SUM OF THE SONS OF KOHATH. First, because of Moses and Aaron.
FROM THIRTY YEARS OLD AND UPWARD. Close to four weeks.
[EVEN UNTIL FIFTY YEARS OLD.] A fifty-year-old is seven weeks of age. The body’s strength then declines.
TO DO WORK IN THE TENT OF MEETING. The work of bearing.
ABOUT THE MOST HOLY THINGS. The reference is to the ark.
THE VEIL OF THE SCREEN. Which covers the ark.
AND SHALL PUT THEREON. On the cover. Others say that the word alav (thereon) refers to the word et (v. 5), which precedes parokhet (the veil). Va-titzpeno (and hid him) (Josh. 2:6) is similar.
AND SHALL SPREAD OVER IT A CLOTH ALL OF BLUE. Kelil tekhelet means all of blue.

OVER IT. Some say, over the covering of tachash (sealskin). However, it appears to me that its meaning is, and they had already spread a cloth all of blue over the screen covering. If the blue cover was used in order to glorify the ark, then the first interpretation appears correct. The tachash covering served to protect [the ark] from the rain and the dust.
AND SHALL SET THE STAVES THEREOF. Note, they removed the staves until the ark was covered. Some say that they shall set the staves upon the shoulders of the bearers.
AND UPON THE TABLE OF SHOWBREAD. To teach us that there were other tables there for the use of the meat. Furthermore, the showbread which was placed upon this table was not removed.

A CLOTH OF SCARLET. Look. There were two cloth coverings plus a covering of skin upon the table. There were similarly a screen covering, a blue cloth covering, and a covering of skin over the ark. A cloth covering and a cover of skin were over the menorah.
AND SHALL PUT IT UPON A BAR. For it did not have any staves. It is similar to and they bore it upon a pole (Num. 13:25).

AND UPON THE GOLDEN ALTAR THEY SHALL SPREAD. Another cloth and a covering.[15.] OF COVERING THE HOLY FURNITURE, AND ALL THE HOLY VESSELS. The ark, the table, the menorah, the altars, and all the utensils of ministry such as the knives, the spoons, and the plates.
AND THEY SHALL TAKE AWAY THE ASHES. It means, and they shall take away the ashes from the altar.
THESE THINGS ARE THE BURDEN OF THE SONS OF KOHATH IN THE TENT OF MEETING. For they did not carry the tent and the tabernacle.
AND THE CHARGE OF. U-fekudat (and the charge of) is related to the word pakid (overseer).

THE OIL FOR THE LIGHT. Some say that Eleazar carried oil for one night’s light and similarly the continual meal offering. However, I believe that Eleazar was in charge of giving the oil for the light , that is, of the utensil containing the oil for the light, and similarly the vessel containing the anointing oil and the vessel containing the sweet incense, to the children of Kohath.

[HE SHALL HAVE THE CHARGE OF ALL THE TABERNACLE.] Scripture states this because Eleazar had charge over the tabernacle along with his brother Ithamar. However, Eleazar alone had charge over the oil, the sweet incense, and the meal offering because of his great status.
[UNTO MOSES AND UNTO AARON.] Scripture states this because Aaron and his sons were commanded to take heed that the sons of Kohath do not come to the penalty of excision ( karet ).
The command Cut ye not off was given to Moses, Aaron and his sons.
THAT THEY MAY LIVE. That their lives may be extended.

AND NOT DIE. By excision. The meaning of our verse is that the family of the Kohathites will be rewarded if they observe and will be punished if they do not. Without the phrase and not die , our verse could be taken to imply that they will not be punished.
AND APPOINT THEM. The ark, the table, the menorah, and the altars.
EVERY ONE TO HIS SERVICE. This refers to the holy vessels.
AND TO HIS BURDEN. To be carried on the shoulder.

BUT THEY SHALL NOT GO IN. The Kohathites shall not go in to the tent of meeting to see the holy things as they are being covered. The meaning of ke-vala et ha-kodesh (the holy things as they are being covered) is, when the structure is taken down, the veil of the curtain is removed and the ark is revealed. Others say that the meaning of ke-vala is, when they are being covered. Thus the meaning of ke-vala et ha-kodesh is, when they cover the ark in order to carry it. This interpretation is more plausible than the first one. Now there are two prohibitions. One, not to touch the holy vessels-they are to be carried only by staves. Two, the Kohathites shall not see the holy things.
TAKE THE SUM. Naso (take the sum) is an infinitive. It is like zakhor (remember) in Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy (Ex. 20:8). The meaning of naso is, take the sum.
ALSO. Because he had already counted the Kohathites.
IN SERVING. To put up the tabernacle, to make the showbread, to slaughter, and to guard.
AND IN BEARING BURDENS. Le-massa (bearing burdens) is an infinitive. Similarly le-massa (causing to set forward) in and for causing the camps to set forward (Num. 10:2). The forms of verbs change.
AND THE COVERING OF SEALSKIN THAT IS ABOVE IT. Scripture is being brief, for it does not mention the ramskin covering. Some say that the two coverings were attached.
AND ALL THE INSTRUMENTS OF THEIR SERVICE. Such as tables, pegs, and cords.
AND WHATSOEVER THERE MAY BE TO DO WITH THEM. The instruments of service, or the tabernacle and the altar.
AS FOR THE SONS OF MERARI. Scripture does not mention that they were counted, for this section is connected to the one above.
THE WORK OF SERVICE. This is to be understood as I have already explained. Now the meaning of All those that were numbered (v. 46) is, all those from thirty years old that were numbered.
EVERY ONE. The reference is to Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

TO HIS SERVICE, AND TO HIS BURDEN. Hence and his numbered follows. The section put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is unclean by the dead (Num. 5:2) follows, because God’s presence was in the camps of Israel when they journeyed and when they rested.

EVERY LEPER, AND EVERY ONE THAT HATH AN ISSUE, AND WHOSOEVER IS UNCLEAN BY THE DEAD. These are states of uncleanliness that last for seven days. They also render others unclean. Therefore a person who had a seminal omission does not leave the camp. Similarly, no place was setaside outside the camp for the performing of bodily functions. On the contrary, each person dug in his own tent as is the custom with all the camps, for there were children among them. Now the section which opens with When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies (Deut. 23:10) speaks of a small camp wherein there are no women, and the ark is among them and they do not surround the ark. [They have to leave the camp], for God’s presence is in the center of any Israelite camp. I will explain this in its proper place.
FEMALE. A woman who has an irregular menstrual flow, a normal menstrual flow, a woman who is a leper or who was made unclean by a dead body.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL DID SO. Immediately, before they journeyed. When the unclean journeyed, they journeyed between the standard of Ephraim and the standard of Dan. The aforementioned is based on logic, for this is not explained in Scripture. The section that begins with When a man or woman [ shall commit any sin that men commit, to commit a trespass against the Lord ] follows the previous chapter because leprosy and unclean issue are brought about by trespassing against the Lord. The reason this section is repeated is that the Torah wants to mention but if the man have no kinsman (v. 8).
THEN THEY SHALL CONFESS. Whichever one it be, a man or a woman.
IN FULL. Be-rosho (in full) means as it is, not less than it is.

AND ADD UNTO IT THE FIFTH PART. If he confesses on his own. However, if there are witnesses then he shall add two fifths. Those who transmitted the law say a fifth of a fifth. Their minds are greater than ours.
THE RESTITUTION…SHALL BE THE LORDS. For he made restitution because of his fear of the Lord.

AND EVERY MAN’S HALLOWED THINGS SHALL BE HIS. Its meaning is that they belong to the one who hallows them. He may give them to any kohen that he wants to. This is noted because Scripture mentions the gifts given to the kohanim .
The portion dealing with a straying wife follows because the straying wife commits a trespass against her husband.
IF ANY MAN’S WIFE GO ASIDE. Tisteh means will go aside from the right way. Similarly seteh (go aside) in Go aside from it (Prov. 4:15).
CARNALLY. Shikhvat zera (carnally) refers to carnal laying. It is called shikhvat zera because its purpose is for seed.
AND IT BE HID. She did not reveal the matter. There is not even one witness through whom she is suspect.
NEITHER SHE BE TAKEN IN THE ACT. By witnesses, men or women, so that she be suspected.
AND THE SPIRIT OF JEALOUSY COME UPON HIM. Ru’ach (spirit) is masculine here. Similarly ru’ach (wind) in and a great and strong wind (I Kings 19:11).
COME. Come upon his mind.
BRING. Against her will.
FOR HER. Aleha (for her) means with her or because of her.

BARLEY MEAL. Our rabbis said, she acted like a beast, let her bring the food of a beast. A free-will meal offering consists of pure wheat flower so that the celebrant will be remembered for good. However, this meal offering recalls a sin, if a sin was committed. Hence it is an inferior offering and consists of barley without oil and without frankincense.
AND THE PRIEST SHALL BRING HER NEAR. Her refers to the meal offering.
AND SET HER BEFORE THE LORD. Before the altar.
HOLY WATER. From the basin, for it has already become holy.
ON THE FLOOR OF THE TABERNACLE. The reference is to the well-known floor. The word afar (dust) has a definite article before it. It refers to the earth which is beneath the floor.

AND LET THE HAIR OF THE WOMAN’S HEAD GO LOOSE. Para (go loose) means he shall uncover. However, I believe that it means he shall take out the hair of the woman, which was covered, and let it go loose.

THE WATER OF BITTERNESS. It is my opinion that the word me (water) is in the construct and the word ha-marim is an adjective. If so, then its secret is known. It is also possible that the waters were so called because of their ultimate taste. Compare, And stripped the naked of their clothing (Job 22:6). And the water that causeth the curse shall enter into her and become bitter (v. 24) is proof of this, for this verse indicates that the oaths , which they that cause the curses refers to, will make the sweet waters bitter.
The word ha-me’arerim (that causeth the curse) is a pi’el . It is like the word erarah (cursed) in which the Lord hath cursed (Gen. 5:29).
[SHALL CAUSE HER TO SWEAR.] Its meaning is that the woman shall answer, Amen, Amen .
IF NO MAN HAVE LAIN WITH THEE. Its meaning is, if another man has not forced himself upon you.
AND IF THOU HAST NOT GONE ASIDE. Willingly. Satit means you have gone aside and committed an unclean act. It is similar to thou shalt not build it of hewn stones (Ex. 20:25).

BE THOU FREE. The meaning of hinnaki is, be thou free. It is similar to and die in the mount (Deut. 32:50). It is possible that the first time Scripture says, and the priest shall cause her to swear means, and the priest shall cause her to swear by invoking God’s name. The second time this phrase is used it means, as Scripture notes, via the curses.
THY THIGH…THY BELLY. They are the neighbors.
TO SWELL. The word tzavah means to swell. The word is not found anywhere else in Scripture.
TO FALL AWAY. The lamed of lanpil (to fall away) is vocalized with a pattach because the heh of the form is missing. The same is true of the word lashmid (to destroy) (Is. 23:11).
AMEN, AMEN. The word amen is repeated for emphasis.
[IN A SCROLL.] They had a specific scroll for curses.
THE MEMORIAL-PART THEREOF. That which served as her memorial, for good or bad in accordance with her deeds.
AND HAVE ACTED UNFAITHFULLY. Va-timal ma’al (and have acted unfaithfully) is to be understood here as I have explained. It refers to something covered.
AND SHALL CONCEIVE SEED. God will give her seed in recompense for the shame which befell her.
SHALL BEAR HER INIQUITY. If she was defiled.

Our verse states, And the man shall be clear from iniquity . For if a spirit of jealousy came upon him she is prohibited to him. He is not allowed to be with her. If he sleeps with her, he is guilty of sin. Some say that the section dealing with the Nazirite follows the section dealing with the wife who is accused of adultery because if the latter was not defiled, then she will have a son who is a Nazirite. However, I believe that the chapter dealing with the Nazirite follows [the chapter dealing with the wife who is accused of adultery] because it lays down the law regarding a female Nazirite who is the reverse of the unfaithful wife. Now wine causes most sins. Furthermore, a woman who does not fix her hair does not seek sexual relations.
SHALL CLEARLY UTTER A VOW. The word yafli means to set aside. On the other hand, it might mean doing something out of the ordinary, for most people follow their lusts.
THE VOW OF A NAZIRITE. Neder nazir means an oath to be a Nazirite, for the word nazir (Nazirite) is an adjective. The word ve-yenazeru (that they separate) (Lev. 22:13) is related to it.

[TO CONSECRATE HIMSELF UNTO THE LORD.] To distance himself from lust. He does this in order to serve God, for wine destroys reason and the proper service of God. I will hint at a secret in the chapter that opens with When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies (Deut. 23:10).

[HE SHALL ABSTAIN FROM WINE AND STRONG DRINK.] Its meaning is, if he took a vow to be a Nazirite and holy, then he shall separate himself from wine and strong drink. According to the transmitters of tradition, shekhar (strong drink) is aged wine. Others say that shekhar is to be taken literally; it refers to any drink that intoxicates a person.

[HE SHALL DRINK NO VINEGAR OF WINE…NEITHER SHALL HE DRINK ANY LIQUOR OF GRAPES, NOR EAT FRESH GRAPES.] This explains the oath. He must distance himself from anything connected to wine. In the account of the wife of Manoah, Scripture states, and eat not any unclean thing (Jud. 13:7). She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the grape-vine (Jud. 13:14).

LIQUOR OF. The word mishrat (liquor of) is not found elsewhere in Scripture. The tav indicates that the word is feminine and is in the construct. Mishrat anavim refers to anything that has been mashed with grapes. Others say that mishrat anavim refers to a cooked drink.

PRESSED GRAPES. The word chartzannim (pressed grapes) is not found anywhere else in Scripture. The same applies to the word zag (grape-stone). The commentaries tells us that chartzannim refers to the outer skin of the grape and zag to the pits. Others say the reverse. According to these interpretations, me-chartzannim (from the pressed grapes) is connected to nothing that is made of the grape-vine . The meaning of our verse is that the Nazirite shall eat nothing made from the grapevine, that is, from these two things.
HE SHALL LET THE LOCKS OF THE HAIR OF HIS HEAD GROW LONG. The word gaddel (grow) is a pi’el infinitive. The meaning of gaddel is, he shall grow.
THAT HE CONSECRATETH. The word hazziro (that he consecrateth) is a hifil infinitive.
A DEAD BODY. The word met (dead) is an adjective describing body ( nefesh ). On the other hand, the word guf (body) is missing from our text.

FOR HIS FATHER, OR FOR HIS MOTHER. And certainly not for his wife, his daughter, and others. Some say that the word nazir (Nazirite) is related to the word nezer (crown). Because his consecration (nezer) unto God is upon his head is proof of this. This interpretation is not farfetched. Note that most people are slaves to worldly lusts. The true king, the one who has a crown, the one who wears the royal diadem, is the person who is free from this lust.
VERY SUDDENLY. The words peta and pitom are close in meaning. The same applies to admat afar (dust of the earth) (Dan. 12:2).
AND HE DEFILE. The corpse will defile him.
IN THE DAY OF HIS CLEANSING. By the waters of purification, for he was defiled by a corpse.
ONE FOR A SIN-OFFERING AND THE OTHER FOR A BURNT-OFFERING. Its secret was explained by the sages. They said that the reward of sin is sin.

FOR THAT HE SINNED BY REASON OF THE BODY. The reference is to a dead body. Compare the word nefesh (body) in Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for a body (Lev. 19:28). If the sin referred to a sin committed against his very own body, then Scripture would not command him to return to his sin.
AND HE SHALL CONSECRATE UNTO THE LORD THE DAYS OF HIS NAZIRITESHIP. All the days that he vowed to be a Nazirite. He shall now begin to count them.
BECAUSE HIS CONSECRATION WAS DEFILED. For he vowed to be a Nazirite for a fixed number of days in succession without anything intervening and breaking them up.

FULFILLED. Melot (fulfilled) is an infinitive. Its final root letter is an alef . It is conjugated like a word that has a heh as a final root letter. It is like the word kero’ot (call) in that thou didst call us (Jud. 8:1).

HE SHALL BRING IT. Yavi oto (he shall bring it) means he shall bring himself. Compare, but the shepherds fed themselves (Ezek. 34:8). Or yavi oto means that the kohen shall bring him against his will by commanding that he be forced to bring his sacrifice.
ONE HE-LAMB. A male, as is the law regarding all burnt offerings.
ONE EWE-LAMB. A female, as is the law with all sin offerings.
AND ONE RAM…FOR PEACE-OFFERINGS. As an expression of joy that he fulfilled his vow.
HIS SIN-OFFERING. The sin offering is mentioned first because it was mentioned last, for this is Hebrew style.
THE HAIR OF. The Hebrew word for hair of is vocalized in two ways.
WHEN IT IS SODDEN. The meaning of beshelah (when it is sodden) is, and it is sodden.

AFTER HE HATH SHAVEN HIS CONSECRATED HEAD. This is a sign that the kodesh hu (this is holy) (v. 20) refers to the word shoulder , for that is the main organ that is being waved. On the other hand, the word hu (this) may refer to all that is waved.

[BESIDE THAT FOR WHICH HIS MEANS SUFFICE.] It means that he is obligated to give in accordance with his wealth. He is also obligated to give in accordance with the days of his vow, whether they are few or whether they are many. The chapter dealing with the blessings of the kohanim follows the chapter dealing with the Nazirite because, after concluding the laws of the Nazirite who is holy, Scripture mentions the laws of the kohanim who are holy. Those who contradict Rabbinic tradition say that the kohen used this blessing to bless all who brought a gift. They claim that the blessing of the kohanim follows the law of the Nazirite because the latter concludes with “beside that which the means of the celebrant suffice.” However, the truth is in keeping with the tradition of our sages of blessed memory. And Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people, and blessed them (Lev. 9:22) on the eighth day is proof of this. This portion was written because God commanded Aaron to bless the people when the tabernacle was erected. Scripture there mentions, nesi’at kappayim (the lifting of the hands), for the word kappayim means the same as yadayim (hands). However, the term yadayim is a more general term.
THE LORD BLESS THEE. The Lord increase your life and your wealth.
AND KEEP THEE. God will protect what he has increased so that no one steals it.

THE LORD MAKE HIS FACE TO SHINE UPON THEE. Its meaning is the same as In the light of the king’s countenance is life (Prov. 16:15). It means may God make his face to shine upon you when you ask something of Him and at the time that you make the request. May God accept you and may His will be to immediately fulfill your request.

[AND BE GRACIOUS TO THEE.] If you make a request of God in a time of trouble, may He be gracious to you. Ve-yechunekka (and be gracious to thee) is similar to channuni (have pity) in have pity upon me, O ye (Job. 19:21) and chanan (graciously given) in The children whom God hath graciously given (Gen. 33:5). Ve-yechunekka comes from the same root as chanan .
THE LORD LIFT UP HIS COUNTENANCE UPON THEE. The reverse of I will hide Mine eyes from you (Is. 1:15). As I have already explained, its meaning is, wherever you go My face shall be lifted up to you.
AND GIVE THEE PEACE. Its meaning is similar to, no evil — from stones, from evil animals, from any enemy — touch thee (Job. 5:19).

SO SHALL THEY PUT MY NAME. Its meaning is similar to to set His name there (Deut. 14:24), that is, the children of Israel be sanctified by God’s name. Or it means that when they shall mention My name over the children of Israel [I will bless them], for God’s revered and awe-inspiring name is found in each one of the three verses.

AND I WILL BLESS THEM. It is possible that the mem of avarekhem (I will bless them) refers to the kohanim who utter the blessing. It means they will bless Israel, and I will bless those who bless. It is also possible that the mem of avarekhem refers to Israel. Its meaning is, if the kohanim bless Israel, then I will bless Israel; that is, I will fulfill the blessing of the kohanim . In my opinion, the mem of avarekhem refers to all of them, the kohanim and the Israelites.

[AND IT CAME TO PASS ON THE DAY THAT MOSES HAD MADE AN END OF SETTING UP THE TABERNACLE.] Moses made an end to the setting up of the tabernacle after the blessing of the kohanim , as this was how events unfolded. On the day that Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them, the dedication of the tabernacle began. The verse And it came to pass on the day that Moses had made an end of setting up the tabernacle is proof of the words of our sages, that Moses took the tabernacle down, raised it up and took it down again, and erected it again throughout the seven days of dedication to train the kohanim . For the meaning of and sanctified them is that he sanctified them [the furniture, the altar, and the vessels] by the sprinkling of the blood during the seven days of dedication.
AND THE ALTAR AND ALL THE VESSELS THEREOF. This is connected to on the day that Moses had made an end of setting up the tabernacle . It means that he set the altar up in its place.
AND ALL THE VESSELS THEREOF, AND HAD ANOINTED THEM. With the anointing oil
AND SANCTIFIED THEM. With blood. Scripture mentions the altar because of its dedication.
THAT THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL…OFFERED. Scripture employs a general term. Its meaning is that they brought their offering to the Lord before the opening of the tabernacle.

COVERED. The word tzav (covered) here is similar to the word tzabbim (Utters) in and in litters, and upon mules (Is. 66:20). The reference is to a type of ox that pulls wagons. Others say that eglot tzav (covered wagons) refers to a wagon that is overloaded and that tzav is connected to the word tzavah (swell) (Num. 5:21). However, this is farfetched.

[AND TWELVE OXEN.] I have already explained in my work Moznayim that the mem in shenem asar (twelve) remains both in the absolute and in the construct. The meaning of shenem asar (twelve) is two ( shenayim ) and ten ( eser ). The word shenem is connected to aser for purposes of brevity. The same applies to shelosh elleh (these three) (Ex. 21:11). The phrase shene asar (twelve) without the mem is an abridged form.
FOR EVERY TWO OF THE PRINCES. Al shene ha-nesi’im means for every two of the princes.

[13. AND HIS OFFERING.] Scripture reads, and his offering because Scripture had already stated, And he that presented [ his offering ] (v. 12). The vav of ve-korbano (and his offering) means, and this was his offering. Scripture writes with regard to the second day, hikriv et korbano (he offered his offering) (v. 18), for this is the style of Scripture. Compare, And Isaac spoke unto Abraham his father, and said: ‘My father ’ (Gen. 22:7). The word father is repeated because Scripture is being lengthy. Then spoke the king Ahasuerus and said unto Esther the queen (Esth. 7:5) is also similar. Scripture does not mention the term hikriv (he presented) with regard to the other princes, for Scripture wanted to be brief. Similarly the term le-gulgelotam (by their poles) is used only in the numbering of Reuben and Simeon. There are many such examples.

ON THE SEVENTH DAY. Some say that Elishama the son of Ammihud presented his offering on the Sabbath. It was a ruling for that time. Others say that the reference is to the seventh day of the dedication of the tabernacle. Those who disagree with our sages say that the first day of the altar’s dedication did not fall on the first day of the week. However, this is of no avail, for it is impossible that there be no Sabbath in twelve days.I believe that the second interpretation is correct, because of the peace offering. The seventh day of the circling of Jericho is similar. Likewise the seven days of the dedication of the temple (I Kings 8:65) because of the Day of Atonement.
ONE YOUNG BULLOCK. Ben bakar means a young bullock. Compare, ben yonah (young dove).

TWO OXEN. These were also male bullocks. The meaning of bakar (oxen) is, from the kind of cattle. And all the oxen for the sacrifice of peace-offerings twenty and four bullocks (v. 88) is proof of this.

ON THE ELEVENTH DAY. I have already explained in my work moznayim why this number differs [from the other numbers]. The word ashte in ( ashte asar , eleven) is similar to the word eshtonotav (his thoughts) (Ps. 146:4). It ( ashte ) refers to that which a person’s thoughts give birth to. The number ten, as it were begets [eleven, etc.]. This is a great secret. Rabbi Jonah the Sephardi says that ashte asar is short for al shete asar . Its meaning is, the number that precedes twelve. Now Rabbi Jonah made two great mistakes. One, contrary to his words, the number twelve is beyond ( al ) the number eleven. From twenty years old and upward (va-ma’alah) (Num. 1:3) is proof of the aforementioned. His second mistake is that if the word ashte is short for al shete , then the text should have read ashne asar , not ashte asar . For ashte is in the feminine. Ashte is therefore one word.

[AND WHEN MOSES WENT IN.] It is likely that the beginning of God’s word to Moses [in the tabernacle], which is what And the Lord called unto Moses (Lev. 1:1) refers to, was uttered when the dedication of the tabernacle was completed. All the grammarians say that the word middabber (speaking) in speaking unto him is a hitpa’el with the tav swallowed. However, in my opinion middadbber is an infinitive. It is similar to the word dabber (speak) in behold, I cannot speak (Jer. 1:5). The mem prefixed to middabber is in place of the word min , as is the rule in the Hebrew language.

The meaning of va-yishma (then he heard) is that only Moses heard the voice. Anyone in the tent of meeting outside of the curtain did not hear the voice. The following is also correct: God made Moses’ ear supersensitive as he added to the sight of Elisha’s young man (II Kings 6:17). Similarly Then the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam (Num. 22:31).
AND HE SPOKE UNTO HIM. This was the way God’s word always came to Moses.
SPEAK UNTO AARON. For he is obligated to fulfill the commandment of lighting the lamps.

IN FRONT OF THE CANDLESTICK. This explains to give light (he’ir) over against it (Ex. 25:37). Now the word he’ir (give light) is transitive. It is similar to the word ta’ir (dost light) in For Thou dost light my light (Ps. 18:29). However, this is not the case with the word ya’iru (shall give light) and the word he’irah (did shine) in and the earth did shine (Ezek. 43:2). This section follows in order to teach that God’s word also came at night, for the light was to burn in the tabernacle and was not to be extinguished.
AND THIS WAS THE WORK OF THE CANDLESTICK. Scripture teaches that no such menorah was ever seen.
BEATEN. I have already explained the meaning of mikshah (beaten).
THE BASE THEREOF. This refers to the shaft upon which it stood, for Scripture explicitly states, its base, and its shaft (Ex. 25:31).

THE FLOWERS THEREOF. The meaning of the word pirchah (flowers thereof) is well known. If God had not shown Moses the menorah in a prophetic vision, then no wise craftsman would have had the ability to make the menorah described in Scripture.
SO HE MADE. This refers to Moses. The meaning of made is, made by command. The same applies to And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold (Ex. 25:31).

The section dealing with the Levites follows the one dealing with the lighting of the menorah to teach us that Aaron shall occupy himself with the kindling of the lamps. However, the Levites shall assist him in the other services and shall stand before him to do all that he commands.
TAKE THE LEVITES FROM AMONG THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. For they were mixed in. The same was true of all the tribes before they journeyed on from Mount Sinai.

THE WATER OF PURIFICATION. Chattat (purification) here is similar to the word techatteni (purify me) (Ps. 51:9). Or it is possible that the me chattat (the water of purification) was similar to a sin offering ( korban chattat ).
SPRINKLE…UPON THEM. Rabbi Moses says that the first root letter of hazzeh (sprinkle) is a nun . Compare, hakkeh takkeh (thou shalt surely smite) (Deut. 13:16). Rabbi Moses is correct.
AND LET THEM CAUSE A RAZOR TO PASS OVER ALL THEIR FLESH. Its meaning is, and they have already caused a razor to pass over their flesh. The sages said even the beard, but not the corner of the beard.
AND LET THEM WASH THEIR CLOTHES. And after this they will be cleansed, being purified by the waters of purification.

[AND CLEANSE THEMSELVES.] The word ve-hitteharu (and cleanse themselves) is a hitpa’el . The tav of the hitpa’el is swallowed. Compare, ha-mitkaddeshim ve-ha-mittaharim (They that sanctify themselves and purify themselves) (Is. 66:17).
A YOUNG BULLOCK. The term ben bakar indicates a young bullock.
FINE FLOUR. Three-tenth parts (of an efah ) as is the law.

SHALT THOU TAKE. By issuing a command, for the Levites shall take. The meaning of Then let them take (ve-lakechu) is, then let them give. Compare, ve-yikechu li terumah (that they take for Me an offering). On the other hand, the meaning of Then let them take might be that they shall take with them. Compare, they shall take (ve-yikechu) to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses (Ex. 12:3).

BEFORE THE LORD. Its meaning is, when you present the Levites before the tent, the Levites shall lay their hands upon the head of each one of the bullocks. There are many similar instances in Scripture.

AND OFFER THOU. Offer by command, for Aaron was the celebrant. Scripture’s statement that the sin offering and also the burnt offering were to make atonement for the Levites is true proof of the aforementioned. Furthermore, Scripture states, and Aaron made an atonement for them (v. 21).
[AND THOU SHALT SET THE LEVITES BEFORE AARON.] After Aaron shall make atonement for the Levites, you shall set them up before Aaron, and Aaron shall offer them for a wave offering.
AND OFFER THEM FOR A WAVE-OFFERING. Via your command. Compare, And offer thou (v. 12).
AND THE LEVITES SHALL BE MINE. This is a great status.
AND AFTER THAT SHALL THE LEVITES GO IN. After you purify them.
AND OFFER THEM. Via your command.

FOR THEY ARE WHOLLY GIVEN UNTO ME. They, and their children, are given unto Me. The Israelites gave them to Me and I took them unto Me ; that is, I accepted them. Why are they given [unto Me]? In order to redeem all that openeth the womb. The word pitrat (openeth) and peter (openeth) are two different words. Compare, tzedek (righteousness) and tzedakah (righteousness). Or they might be the same word in two paradigms.
ON THE DAY THAT I SMOTE. The word yom (day) means time. Compare, Thou art this day (yom) to pass over (Deut. 2:18).

[AND I HAVE TAKEN THE LEVITES.] Scripture has already stated, have I taken them unto Me (v. 16). This is the style of Scripture. And I have taken the Levites is connected to the verse which follows. It means, when I took the Levites, I gave them to Aaron and his sons (v. 19).
AND TO MAKE ATONEMENT. To be an atonement for the souls of the children of Israel, as I have already explained.
THUS DID MOSES AND AARON. Moses by command, Aaron by waving them, and Israel by the laying of their hands on them.
[AND THE LEVITES PURIFIED THEMSELVES.] Scripture tells us that they also performed [purification rituals].

AND AARON MADE ATONEMENT FOR THEM. And Aaron had already made atonement for them. Others say that the Levites first purified themselves and afterwards laid their hands on the bullocks. This interpretation is not far off the mark. If this is so, then the meaning of And thou shalt set the Levites (v. 13) is: and you have already set the Levites at the beginning.
SO DID THEY UNTO THEM. So did the sons of Aaron always unto the children of the Levites.

THIS IS THAT WHICH PERTAINETH UNTO THE LEVITES. Its meaning is, this is the set time of service which pertains to the Levites. The verse reading from thirty years and upward (Num. 4:23) does not contradict our verse, for from thirty years and upward refers to the service of bearing burdens (Num. 4:24), while our verse, which reads from twenty and five years all and upward , refers to the service in the work of the tent of meeting.
The meaning of li-tzeva (to perform the service) is, to be counted among the host of workers.

TO KEEP THE CHARGE. This command is directed to the elders. The section dealing with the Passover follows the section dealing with the consecration of the Levites because the dedication of the altar took place in the first month. The Levites were separated at that time. The section dealing with Passover is written here because, concerning the Passover, it was written, And it shall come to pass, when ye be come to the land (Ex. 12:25); And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land (Ex. 13:5). This chapter records that God commanded that they were obligated to offer the Passover sacrifice in the desert also.
BUT THERE WERE CERTAIN MEN. It is impossible for a camp to be big as that of the Israelites without people dying every day.
WHEREFORE ARE WE TO BE KEPT BACK. Niggara (kept back) is a nifal .
STAY YE. At the opening of the tent of meeting.
IN A JOURNEY AFAR OFF. We do not have to search for the meaning of this phrase, for our sages have already transmitted to us the meaning of afar off .
OF YOU. This refers to being unclean by reason of a dead body.
OR OF YOUR GENERATIONS. This refers to both a person who is unclean by reason of a dead body and to one in a journey far off.
AND IS NOT ON A JOURNEY. U-ve-derekh (and on a journey) is to be rendered, or is on a journey. U-makkeh aviv ve-immo (and he that smiteth his father, or his mother) (Ex. 21:15) is similar.
SHALL BEAR HIS SIN. He alone.
AND IF A STRANGER SHALL SOJOURN AMONG YOU. He too shall observe the second Passover in accordance with the ordinance. Others say that the reference is to the first Passover.

AND ON THE DAY THAT THE TABERNACLE WAS REARED UP. Scripture begins to count the journeys of Israel. It was thus compelled to make mention of the cloud that rested on the tabernacle, for when it camped they camped and when it journeyed they journeyed.
EVEN THE TENT OF THE TESTIMONY. Le-ohel (even the tent) is to be rendered, on the tent. There are many such instances in Scripture.
AT THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED. Its meaning is clear, for God caused the cloud to rest and God caused it to journey.

AND WHEN THE CLOUD TARRIED. The meaning of u- ve-ha’arikh (and when it tarried) is to be rendered, and if it tarried. Scripture first speaks in general terms. It then goes on to say that sometimes the Israelites would journey for a few days or encamp according to the commandment of the Lord.

OR IF IT CONTINUED BY DAY AND BY NIGHT. They thus occasionally journeyed at night. Others say that yomam va-laylah (by day and by night) is to be interpreted literally. This interpretation appears correct to me. The term yomayim (two days) (v. 22) is proof that this interpretation is correct.
OR A YEAR. The word yomam means a full year.
AT THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD THEY ENCAMPED. This is stated at the end of the chapter to indicate that this was the procedure as long as Israel lived in the wilderness.
MAKE THEE TWO TRUMPETS OF SILVER. Chatzotzerot (trumpets) is a noun. In its verbal form, one of the tzadis is not pronounced even though it is written.

FOR THE CALLING. Le-mikra (for the calling) is an infinitive. The same applies to u-le-massa (and for causing to set forward). On the other hand, they might be nouns. In this case, the word le-mikra (for the calling) means at the time of calling, and le-massa (and for causing to set forward), at the time of journeying. The first interpretation appears correct to me.

AND WHEN THEY SHALL BLOW WITH THEM. And when the trumpeters shall blow with them. It is similar to and he said to Joseph (Gen. 48:1) and whom she bore to Levi (Num. 26:59). Now its meaning is, if they blow both trumpets, then the princes and the congregation shall gather.

AND IF THEY BLOW BUT WITH ONE. This means if they blow with one trumpet, then the princes alone shall come. If a tru’ah (an alarm) sounds, then the standard of Judah shall journey, even though the cloud is upon the tabernacle. In the opinion of many, another cloud journeyed before the Israelites.
THE CAMPS THAT LIE ON THE EAST SIDE SHALL TAKE THEIR JOURNEY. For they consisted of three camps.

AN ALARM THE SECOND TIME. So that the standard of Reuben will take up its journey. They did not blow the trumpets again, for the family of Kohath and with them the kohanim who blew the trumpets journeyed before the standard of Ephraim.
THEY SHALL BLOW AN ALARM FOR THEIR JOURNEYS. The kohanim shall blow an alarm for their journeys, for they journeyed after the standard of Reuben.

AND THEY SHALL BE TO YOU FOR A STATUTE FOR EVER. The camps now journeyed to battle. Is this not Moses’ words when the ark journeyed? Note that Scripture explains this statute. It says that Israel shall do the following: The kohanim shall sound the alarm upon trumpets when Israel goes forth to war, to battle in the land of their enemies, and similarly if an enemy enters their land and Israel goes forth to fight them.
AND YE SHALL BE REMEMBERED. For you have done what God the glorious commanded you do. The alarm ( tru’ah ) also serves as a reminder to the people to cry out to God.

ALSO IN THE DAY OF YOUR GLADNESS, AND IN YOUR APPOINTED SEASONS. When you return from the land of your enemies, or you defeat the enemy who attacks you and you establish a day of rejoicing, such as the days of Purim or the seven days of rejoicing in the days of Hezekiah. However, our transmitters of tradition explained that the day of your gladness refers to the Sabbath. The trumpets were sounded so that Israel would hear that the burnt offerings were being offered and that they should direct their hearts to God.
ON THE TWENTIETH DAY OF THE MONTH. The standards first journeyed on this day. Thus Israel was at Sinai close to a year.
BY THEIR STAGES. As it was fit for them to journey.
AND THE CLOUD ABODE IN THE WILDERNESS OF PARAN. I will explain this and, And they took their first journey (v. 13) later.
TAKEN DOWN. The Levites took it down.
THE BEARERS OF THE SANCTUARY. The reference is to the ark.
MIGHT BE SET UP. That the Gershonites and the Merarites might set up the tabernacle before the coming of the Kohathites so that the kohanim could immediately bring the ark into its place.
REARWARD. According to the standards, for Naphtali was last.
THUS WERE THE JOURNEYINGS OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. Its meaning is, thus did they journey all the days that they were in the wilderness.

[29. AND MOSES SAID UNTO HOBAB, THE SON OF REUEL.] We find Scripture telling us that Zipporah was the daughter of Reuel, for it is written, and he [Reuel] gave Moses Zipporah his daughter (Ex. 2:21). Furthermore, Scripture states, to water their father’s flock (Ex. 2:16), and to Reuel their father (Ex. 2:18). Now Hobab was the son of Reuel. Thus Hobab was the brother of Zipporah. According to a rational analysis of Scripture, Hobab is to be identified with Jethro, because the Torah states, as thou [Hobab] knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness (v. 31) and it states with regard to Jethro when he came to the wilderness, into the wilderness where he was encamped (Ex. 18:5). Should one disagree and argue that Scripture refers to Jethro as choten mosheh (Moses’ father-in-law) (Ex. 18:1), then one can respond that it is the way of Scripture to refer to the father and the brother of a young woman by the term choten (father-in-law). Unto Hobab, the son of Reuel…choten mosheh (Moses’ father-in-law) is proof of the aforementioned. For it has already been made clear to you that Hobab was the brother of Zipporah, and Scripture calls him choten mosheh (Moses’ father-in-law). Should one argue that choten mosheh (Moses’ father-in-law) is not connected to Hobab but to Reuel, then the response is, Scripture explicitly states Hobab choten mosheh (the father-in-law of Moses) (Jud. 4:11). Many say that Hobab and Jethro are one and the same. They maintain that Jethro/Hobab was the father of Zipporah and that Reuel was the grandfather of Zipporah. They argue that Scripture says, to Reuel their father (Ex. 2:18) in the same manner that Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham (Gen. 32:10). Scripture similarly refers to Zipporah as Reuel’s daughter in the same manner that it refers to Belshazzar as Nebuchadnezzar’s son, when in fact he was Nebuchadnezzar’s grandson. Our sages say that Jethro had seven names. There are seventy faces to the Torah.
TO MINE OWN LAND, AND TO MY KINDRED. Where I was born and where I live unto this very day.
LEAVE US NOT, I PRAY THEE. The word na (I pray thee) means now. The same applies to the word na in all of Scripture. The opposite is the case in Arabic.

FORASMUCH AS THOU KNOWEST. Ki al ken (forasmuch) here means the same as ki al ken in forasmuch as I gave her not to Shelah my son (Gen. 38:26). Since ( ki al ken ) you know the place where we encamped, come with us.

AND THOU SHALT BE TO US INSTEAD OF EYES. You will show us the way. Many say that ve-hayita (and thou shalt be) is to be taken as a perfect and alludes to the advice which Jethro gave Moses. He showed Moses what Moses did not know. They say this is what eyes refers to.
The meaning of And he said: Leave us not, I pray thee is, and he had already said to him [leave us not I pray thee] but it was to no avail.

[33. AND THEY SET FORWARD FROM THE MOUNT OF THE LORD THREE DAYS’ JOURNEY.] In my opinion the first journey was unlike the rest of the journeys. The verse which states, and the Kohathites…set forward (v. 21) after the two standards journeyed refers to all the other journeys except this one, for the ark journeyed before the camp of the Israelites. However, this was the case for only three days. This is the meaning of three days (v. 33). Similarly, And they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham (Num. 33:8) does not mean that they traveled a three days journey in one day. Others say that they traveled a three-day journey in one day. Others say that they traveled a journey of three days corresponding to the journeys when they left Egypt, and the ark was a three-day distance from them. This is the meaning of and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran (v. 12). They explain that And they took their first journey (v. 13), means that they journeyed by the command of Moses, for the cloud traveled immediately. However, this is not so, for Moses did not distance himself from the ark, as proved by And it came to pass, when the ark set forward (v. 35) And when it rested (v. 36). What I said above appears correct to me. Paran , in and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran (v. 12), is a general name for Taberah, which is the same as Kibroth-hattaavah (v. 34), Hazeroth (Num. 33:17), Rithmah (Num. 33:18), and many other journeys. The fact that Scripture does not mention the wilderness of Paran in the Torah portion Elleh Mase (these are the stages) is proof of this. I will explain this later.
The meaning of according to the commandment of the Lord (v. 13) is, when the trumpets sounded the alarm.
RISE UP, O LORD. As people do when they rise up to battle.
[BE SCATTERED.] When Your enemies see that You arose to do battle, they will immediately be scattered.
[THEM THAT HATE THEE.] The word mesanekha (them that hate Thee) is a pi’el . The nun does not receive a dagesh in order to simplify the enunciation of the word.
SCATTERED…FLEE. Scripture repeats itself as is its style in all prophecies, as I will explain in the portion dealing with Balaam.

AND WHEN IT RESTED. When the ark rested. U-venucho (when it rested) is spelled with a heh in the same way that the word oholo (his tent) (Gen. 13:3) is, for the letters alef, heh, vav, yod interchange.

RETURN, O LORD. Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, says that every time the word shav in the kal conjugation is related in meaning to teshuvah (return), it is intransitive, not transitive. However, when it means peace and quiet, as in in sitting still (be-shuvah) and rest shall ye be saved (Is. 30:15), and similarly in Return (shuvah), O Lord, unto the ten thousands of the families of Israel , it means that God will give them rest and they will not be disturbed by any enemy. Note, the word revavah (ten thousand) comes from the same root as the word rav (many). Revavah in our verse is similar to the word revavah (increase) in I cause thee to increase (Ezek. 16:7). It is possible that ten thousand is called a revavah because it is a great number. The word revavah is therefore connected to the word alfe (thousands). Moses prayed that God would grant rest and quiet to all of Israel, though they be many.
AND THE PEOPLE. This chapter is connected to the one before, because the Israelites camped in kibroth-hatta’avah after the ark journeyed from Sinai. Scripture now tells what happened there.
AS MURMURERS. Mitonenim (murmurers) is related to the word aven (evil). Onekh (evil) in thy evil (onekh) thoughts (Jer. 4:14) is similar.
[AND WHEN THE LORD HEARD.] The meaning of when the Lord heard is, and when the Lord heard that they spoke evil.

AND DEVOURED. Va-tokhal (and devoured) is penultimately accented. Compare, va-yomer (and he said) (Gen. 14:19). However, when it ends a clause, then it is ultimately accented. The latter is contrary to the laws of Hebrew grammar, but we find it to be so.
AND THE PEOPLE CRIED UNTO MOSES. In a conciliatory manner.
AND THE FIRE ABATED. Va-tishka (abated) means extinguished. The word is not used again in Scripture with this meaning.
TABERAH. I will explain this term later.

AND THE MIXED MULTITUDE. Who were gathered unto the children of Israel but were not of Israelite stock. The asafsuf (the mixed multitude) refers to the erev rav (the mixed multitude). The word is constructed by doubling two root letters. Compare, secharchar (fluttereth) (Ps. 38:11) and chamarmaru (burn) (Lam. 1:20).
AND…WEPT. After they lusted.
THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL…ON THEIR PART. With them.
THE FISH. The word dagah (fish) is a general term.
FOR NOUGHT. Cheaply, as if we got it for nothing.

THE CUCUMBERS. An alef has been substituted for a heh in the word kishu’im (cucumbers), for kishu’im is related to the word mikshah (cucumber) (Is. 1:8). Compare, telu’im (suspense) in And My people are in suspense about returning to Me (Hos. 11:7). There are many such instances.
MELONS. We can ascertain the meaning of avatichim (melons) from Arabic. It has no cognate in Scripture.

AND THE LEEKS. The word chatzir (leeks) refers to vegetables, which are the grass of the field. Compare, Who maketh the mountains to spring with grass (chatzir) (Ps. 147:8). Chatzir is thus an all-inclusive noun. However, the Aramaic translation says that it refers to a specific kind. It too is correct.
AND THE ONIONS, AND THE GARLIC. The meaning be-tzalim (onions) and shumim (garlic) is known. They have similar names in Arabic.
BUT NOW OUR SOUL IS DRIED AWAY. The reference is to the lusting soul, which is implanted in the liver.
THERE IS NOTHING AT ALL. We lack everything.
TO LOOK TO. For the manna came down from heaven.

NOW THE MANNA. Scripture describes the stupidity of those who lusted, for the manna was like coriander seed, which is easy to pick, and it was easy to see, for it was white. Furthermore, they could eat it as it was. They could also grind it in mills and make cakes out of it. They could also beat it in mortars and cook it in pots. It had an especially good taste, for it tasted like [food] with the finest oil. Additionally, it came down after the dew had washed the place [upon which it fell]. It thus descended upon a clean place.
LIKE CORIANDER SEED. Zera (seed) is in the construct. It is like the word neta (plant of) in the plant of His delight (Is. 5:7).
CORIANDER. Some identify this with kusbarta . Others say that it refers to mustard. They connect gad (coriander) with the word gidin (sinews). However, I do not know its meaning.

THE PEOPLE WENT ABOUT. The word shatu (went about) is related to the word shut (going to and fro) in From going to and fro (mi-shut) in the earth (Job 1:7). This shows that the individual pieces of manna did not fall in one place but were spread and scattered.
IN MILLS. Operated by hand. The word rechayim (mills) does not come in the singular, for a mill consists of two parts.
IN MORTARS. A vessel made out of wood or stone. It is called a medocha (mortars) because they pound in it. It was also possible to make cakes from what they pounded.
AND MADE CAKES. Compare, and make cakes (Gen. 18:6).

A CAKE. Some say that the lamed of leshad (cake) is superfluous. It is similar to the lamed of shalanan (at ease) in at ease and quiet (Job 21:23). The word ha-shamen (with oil) should have been ultimately accented because the word shamen (oil) is an adjective. However, I believe that the lamed of leshad is a root letter. The word leshad is similar to the word leshadi (my sap) in My sap was turned (Ps. 32:4). My (leshadi) sap stands in contrast to the droughts (charvone) in the droughts of summer ( Ibid .) . Leshad refers to the finest part of the oil that floats on top of all oil. In this case, the word ha-shamen is penultimately vocalized in accordance with the meaning of the word.
WEEPING, FAMILY BY FAMILY. The families gathered together to cry, as they do when they mourn for the dead.
EVERY MAN AT THE DOOR OF HIS TENT. In public.
AND MOSES WAS DISPLEASED. The word ra (displeased) is a perfect. On the other hand, the word hayah (was) might be missing in our text.
WHEREFORE HAST THOU DEALT ILL WITH THY SERVANT. Scripture describes an impetuous action.
AND WHEREFORE HAVE I NOT FOUND FAVOUR IN THY SIGHT. When I said, send, I pray Thee, by the hand of him whom Thou wilt send (Ex. 4:13).
The word matzati (found) is missing an alef . There are many such instances. There is nothing to wonder about when king Yehu is missing.
HAVE I CONCEIVED. Am I their mother?
HAVE I BROUGHT THEM FORTH. Or am I their father? Yelidtihu (brought them forth) is like the word yalad (begot) in and Shelah begot Eber (Gen. 10:24).
CARRY THEM. Until they come to the land.

WHENCE. When the word ayin has a mem prefixed to it, it means from which place. When ayin appears without a mem prefixed to it, it means no. We also find the following clause, Behold, ye are nothing (me-ayin) (Is. 41:24).

BECAUSE IT IS TOO HEAVY FOR ME. The word kaved (heavy) is a verb in the perfect. Compare, zaken (was old) in And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old (Gen. 27:1). On the other hand, the word hu (it) might be missing from our text.
THOU. The word at (Thou) is used for both males and females. It is like lakh (to you), bakh (in you), immakh (with you), and ittakh (with you). However, attah (you) is only used for males.
KILL ME. Horgeni (kill me) means put me to death. Do this to me because of Your righteousness and my request. This is the meaning of if I have found favour in Thy sight .
AND LET ME NOT LOOK. Anymore upon the evil circumstances in which I find myself. There is no need for any scribal emendation.

GATHER UNTO ME. The word esfah (gather) is irregular. It is possible that this is so because of the guttural. Erkhah (set in order) in Set thy words in order before me, stand forth ((Job 33:5) is similar.
AND OFFICERS. For there are elders who are advanced in age but are unfit to be officers. There are also officers who are not elders.
AND I WILL COME DOWN. God’s glory descended in fire in the midst of the cloud.
AND SPEAK WITH THEE THERE. When you hear the voice they will also hear.

AND I WILL TAKE OF THE SPIRIT. The meaning of ve-atzalti (and I will take of the spirit) is, I will take from that which you possess. Note that spirit means wisdom. If some of the wisdom of Reuben is given to Simeon, Reuben’s wisdom is not diminished. It remains as is. Let the light of a candle serve as an example.
SANCTIFY YOURSELVES. Words from the root of kodesh (to sanctify) are found in the positive and the negative. Ha-yikdash (Haggai 2:12), which means shall it be unclean , is similar.
NOR TWO DAYS. Twice as much.
NOR FIVE DAYS. Corresponding to the fingers of the hand of those who eat.

NEITHER TEN DAYS. Twice the amount, corresponding to the fingers of the two hands of those who eat. Nor twenty days has a similar meaning. This may be compared to the saying: Let him eat with the fingers of his hands and with the toes of his feet.

BUT A WHOLE MONTH. I have already explained the meaning of the word chodesh yamim (a whole month). The phrase chodesh yamim alludes to the time that it takes for the moon’s light to return to its original amount. Shenatayim yamim (two full years) (Gen. 41:1) is similar to chodesh yamim .
[AT YOUR NOSTRILS.] The sense of smell is located in the nose. The sense of smell will depart from your nostrils, and will not be found there.

AND IT BE LOATHSOME. The word le-zara is spelled with an alef in place of the heh . Compare, mara in call me Mara (Ruth 1:20), for the letters alef, heh, vav, yod interchange. The word zara (loathsome) refers to something which is strange and abhorrent to the nature of a person who is not used to it.

SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND MEN ON FOOT. There is no need to mention the lesser ones. Many interpret this section in various ways. Some say that Moses paraphrased what the children of Israel would say to him. When they would ask, what sort of meat, Moses would answer them, you have no need to ask, for is the Lord’s hand waxed short ?I do not know why we must suffer in this manner. The text must be interpreted according to its plain meaning. Moses did not know that God would create a sign or a miracle. He thought, as I will explain, that he would do so only to justify his prophet.

WILL THEY SUFFICE THEM. U-matza la-hem (will they suffice them) is to be interpreted as in the Aramaic translation. How precious is the interpretation of our ancients to the effect that the word yishachet (be slain) applies to cattle, and ya’asef (be gathered) refers to fish.
WHETHER MY WORD SHALL COME TO PASS, The word ha-yikrekha (shall come to pass) is similar to va-yiker mikrehah (and her hap was) (Ruth 2:3).
AND MOSES WENT OUT. From the tent of meeting.
AND TOOK OF THE SPIRIT. In my opinion, the word va-yatzel (and took of the spirit) is a hifil .
[AND THEY PROPHESIED.] The vav of va-yitnabbe’u (and they prophesied) is like an unaspirated fa in Arabic.

BUT THY DID SO NO MORE. A second time. The same applies to the phrase ve-lo yasaf (and it went on no more) in with a great voice, and it went on no more (Deut. 5:19) and ve-lo yasaf (now more) in and he knew her again no more (Gen. 38:26). According to the rules of Hebrew grammar, the word yasaf is not related to the word tissafu (swept away) in lest ye be swept away in all their sins (Num. 16:26). Our sages of blessed memory say that Moses took six men from each tribe. Their number thus came to seventy-two. However, Moses dropped the two because God told him to gather seventy men. This is correct.
AND THEY WERE OF THEM THAT WERE RECORDED. At first.
BUT HAD NOT GONE OUT. From the camp of Israel to the tent of meeting.

AND THERE RAN A YOUNG MAN. The word na’ar (young man) has the definite article prefixed to it because it refers to the young man who, aside from Joshua, was known to serve Moses. For Joshua’s service was not the usual service rendered by young men.

FROM HIS YOUTH UP. Some say that the meaning of mi-bechurav (from his youth up) is, from his youth. It means that he did not speak as an elder speaks. Others connect mi-bechurav (from his youth up) to mesharet mosheh (the minister of Moses); this means the one who served Moses from the time of his youth. However, this is incorrect, for this event occurred in the second year. In my opinion, the word mi-bechurav means from the chosen. It means that he was one of those chosen to serve Moses, for there were others with him. Note that the word bachur (youth, or chosen) sometimes changes in the plural and sometimes does not. The same applies to the word saris (officer). It is also possible that they belong to two different paradigms.
SHUT THEM IN. The lamed of kela’em (shut them in) is vocalized with a pattach because a guttural follows it.

[ART THOU JEALOUS.] The heh of ha-mekanne (art thou jealous) is vocalized with a pattach . However, it should have been vocalized with a sheva and a pattach . It was so vocalized because the mem has a sheva na beneath it and two sheva nas are never joined together.
[WOULD THAT.] Mi yitten (would that) is an expression of desire here. It is like saying, who will grant me this request and desire?
AND MOSES WITHDREW. Moses accompanied the elders in order to honor them.
AND THERE WENT FORTH A WIND. On the second day.

AND BROUGHT ACROSS. The word va-gaz (brought across) means cut. It is similar to the word gazi (cut) in Cut off thy hair (Jer. 7:29). The word gez (cutting) in and the first of the cutting of thy sheep (Deut. 18:4) is related to it.

Scripture reads, and cut , because the quail on the shore of the sea were as numerous as the [grains of] sand. Thus God cut off some of the quail from them. Va-yagaz comes from a double root. It is like the word va-yacham (waxed warm) in and the flesh of the child waxed warm (II Kings 4:34).

AND LET THEM FALL. The meaning of va-yittosh (and let them fall) is, and they spread . The quail were spread [all around the camp] and did not have the strength to fly away. Compare, they were spread (netushim) abroad all over the ground (I Sam. 30:16).
ROUND ABOUT THE CAMP. Only. In addition to being spread about the camp, the quail were always about two cubits above the high and low ground.
AND THEY SPREAD. Va-yishtechu means, and they spread. Shittachti (I have spread) in I have spread forth my hands unto Thee (Ps. 88:10) is similar even though they belong to two different forms.
WITH A VERY GREAT PLAGUE. It was the plague of murrain.
WAS CALLED. By someone or by Moses.
THEY BURIED. Those who bury. Compare, And said to Jacob (Gen. 48:1).
THE PEOPLE JOURNEYED UNTO HAZEROTH. Chatzerot (Hazeroth) is to be interpreted as unto Chatzerot. Scripture is being brief.
And they abode at Hazeroth is connected to And…Miriam spoke (12:1), for they abode there on her account. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.
